C-RECORD-PARSE.IntentSummary: Convert the record engine from regex-over-XML to parse-and-splice per the approved spec. One stage captures the pre-conversion world before any conversion lands: a deterministic fixture builder that materializes the real record and the full archive tree from the git object store at the spec's base commit 49b4ebb7c6627601ca77ca384f7b6e205d1f65ed, the shipped engine's golden move outputs stored byte-for-byte under scripts/fixtures/record-parse/golden/, and both discriminating probes reproduced failing against the shipped engine in scripts/fixtures/record-parse/baseline-probes.json. Then the span capability lands in src/artifact/xml.ts with its suite; the minimal record-shape- check ships in the same stage as the capability, because span pairing is well defined only under it; reads convert to the parsed tree next; writes convert last, positioned by parser-derived spans so byte preservation is testable against the goldens; then the archived-spec prose pass is removed from derivePayerMap and both probes are inherited as permanent tests; a final task drives the whole product and pins the byte diffs against the named base commit. Reads convert before writes so every write is positioned by the parser rather than by a pattern. DurableScope anchors exactly the one graph module the spec enumerates — the LINKS target of src/artifact/xml.ts; no other graph module is written and no synthetic module is minted for the scripts/ files, which are in .ngrace-lint.json ignoredDirs and have no owning module. ObservedWriteScope is src/artifact/xml.ts, src/artifact/xml.test.ts, scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts, scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts, the fixture builder, the baseline evidence files, and the seven golden outputs under scripts/fixtures/record-parse/. Do not add spec.xml, plan.xml, or anything under docs/plans/ or .ngrace/changes/archive/. No task carries a Satisfies element: every AC-* in the approved spec carries a complete CloseEvidence child, the shipped rule treats that as the third state that is not a forgotten mapping, and a Satisfies of a close-bound criterion is the error change.close-evidence-and-satisfied. No task Verification and no TargetAssertions command contains a current-mode lint of this project root — no Command text contains --assertions current and none invokes ngrace lint or bun ./src/grace.ts lint of this root while omitting --assertions — because the shipped detector misses the house form bun ./src/grace.ts lint (F171); this rule is stated once here and governs every task below; current-mode lint appears only as the post-archive CloseEvidence of AC-CLOSE-LINT. The payer-phrase pattern PAID_FINDING_RE is named by identifier only; its prose form appears nowhere in this plan. The parked branch c-payment-record-3 is read only through git show of its spec, never checked out, merged or modified; its spec's bytes are captured once into scripts/fixtures/record-parse/parked-spec.xml so no test depends on the branch after baseline. Every new test that spawns a process or measures the real repository carries an explicit generous timeout (F185). Every diff-based criterion names the base commit in prose and in command, and its can-fail direction is demonstrated in the baseline. bun test green is a precondition, never the evidence; the probes are the evidence.

T-001.Title: Capture the pre-conversion world: fixture builder, shipped-engine goldens, both probes reproduced failing, payer-map baseline

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Create scripts/fixtures/record-parse/build-fixture.ts, a deterministic builder that materializes a throwaway fixture root from the git object store at 49b4ebb7c6627601ca77ca384f7b6e205d1f65ed — never from the live working tree, so the fixture is identical at baseline, mid-bundle and post-archive: the whole docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/ directory (the seven record XML files, the stub and the inventory) and the whole .ngrace/changes/archive/ tree at that commit. Flags: --c-selection-row inserts one deterministic live chartered row named C-SELECTION whose Pays element names F21 (an archive directory with no row in either layer at that commit); --f21-tag=single-quoted|spaced|reordered rewrites f21's open tag accordingly, each variant valid XML that parses identically; --parked-spec copies the parked bundle's approved spec, read once via git show c-payment-record-3:.ngrace/changes/active/C-PAYMENT-RECORD-3/spec.xml and stored as scripts/fixtures/record-parse/parked-spec.xml, into the fixture as archive event C-PAYMENT-RECORD-3 — the branch is never checked out, merged or modified. The builder never writes inside this repository except its declared output files under scripts/fixtures/record-parse/.

In the same task, before any conversion task runs, capture the baseline: run the shipped engine's --retire against the --c-selection-row fixture in a temporary root and copy the seven record files it writes byte-for-byte into scripts/fixtures/record-parse/golden/ (findings.xml, findings-retired.xml, rulings.xml, rulings-retired.xml, registry.xml, registry-retired.xml, decisions.xml — the engine's complete write set for a move); and write scripts/fixtures/record-parse/baseline-probes.json recording, each with the rule, the command and the measured result: (1) the false-payment probe against the shipped engine — the fixture with the parked spec validates exit 1 with 15 finding-eligible-still-live errors all naming archive event C-PAYMENT-RECORD-3 including f21 and f21-correction, and --retire then reports moved 15 and stamps PaidBy C-PAYMENT-RECORD-3 on all 15 moved elements, while the same fixture without the parked spec validates exit 0; (2) the equivalence-class probe against the shipped engine — validate and --retire over the four f21-tag variants, unmodified moved 3 with post-move validation exit 0, single-quoted and spaced each moved 2 with f21 left live, a status-file-mismatch on perfectly parsed XML, and a post-move validation that no operation can resolve, reordered moved 3; (3) the payer-map baseline — derivePayerMap imported from the shipped engine and run over the real record and real archive at the base commit, with the token-to-payer map recorded in full, including that F152 and F43 are prose-route only and that F161, F130, F149, F150 and F147 hold row routes; (4) the can-fail demonstrations for the diff criteria — on a throwaway clone at the base commit, one byte appended to one record path and one to README.md, committed: the base-less git diff --exit-code form over those paths exits 0 against that committed drift while the form naming 49b4ebb7c6627601ca77ca384f7b6e205d1f65ed exits 1, and both exit 0 on the clean tree. Extend scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts with a golden comparison test — build the --c-selection-row fixture in a temporary root, run the engine from the repository tree by spawnSync, and byte-compare all seven written files against golden/ — and a baseline-evidence test asserting the recorded failure signatures in baseline-probes.json. Both tests carry explicit generous timeouts (F185). The golden test passes against the shipped engine at capture time and must keep passing after every later task; it is the byte-preservation tripwire, not a target-state criterion. Scratch work in temporary directories, never the working tree.

The capture is complete before any conversion: the seven golden files exist and are non-empty, baseline-probes.json records every result named above, and parked-spec.xml is byte-identical to git show c-payment-record-3:.ngrace/changes/active/C-PAYMENT-RECORD-3/spec.xml. Failure: any conversion task started before these files exist.

T-002.Title: Add the parser-derived source-span capability to the shared XML adapter with its suite

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: src/artifact/xml.ts gains one exported capability, computeElementSpans(text, parsed): given the original XML text and its parseGraceXmlArtifact tree, it returns each element's open-tag byte range and close-tag byte range, computed by pairing the parser's document-order elements with a bounded open-tag scan of the source — an open-tag pattern of the form <Tag\b[^>]*>, quote-aware; self-closing elements carry an open range only. The pairing is verified against the parser at construction: element counts must agree per tag and every parsed attribute must be found inside its element's open-tag bytes; any disagreement raises a loud error naming the disagreement instead of returning spans, and there is no fallback path. No reserialization: the parse output, the GraceXmlNode tree and every existing consumer are unchanged; the capability is additive. Add the export to the START_MODULE_MAP block (the file's MAP_MODE is EXPORTS); the MODULE_CONTRACT LINKS header already names the module and is not edited. This task does not touch scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts.

src/artifact/xml.test.ts gains the capability's suite: for synthetic documents with known offsets, open and close ranges are correct against hand-computed byte positions; for the real record files read at their committed bytes, pairing agrees per tag with the parser across findings.xml (213 Finding elements), findings-retired.xml (58), rulings.xml (61), rulings-retired.xml (5), registry.xml (12), registry-retired.xml (36) and the index's 337 self-closing Entry elements through the self-closing branch; self-closing elements carry open ranges only; a document that mis-pairs raises the loud error; and parsed attributes are located inside their element's open-tag bytes. Counts re-measured at this task's base; the re-measured numbers win if they differ from the ones written here. Explicit generous timeouts where the real files are read (F185).

T-003.Title: Ship the minimal record-shape- check in the engine, in the same stage as the span capability

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts gains the minimal shape check, run on the parsed tree for each of the seven record files, erroring with a code prefixed record-shape- when: the root element is not the expected genre root (Findings for the findings pair, Rulings for the rulings pair, Registry for the registry pair, RecordIndex for the index); a Finding, Decision, Row or Entry element appears anywhere except as a direct child of the root; or any of those elements has a same-tag descendant. Each refuse case is a valid XML document that today's checks accept — parseRecordRoot compares no tag today, and the regex path is blind to nesting — so the check discriminates. This is the load-bearing minimum that makes span pairing well defined, not the full schema: no required-children, depth-beyond-same-tag or allowed-children checks. Clean fixtures validate green. Extend scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts with one fixture per refuse case, each on its own isolated temporary root, plus the clean control, with explicit generous timeouts where processes are spawned (F185).

T-004.Title: Convert every structural read in the engine to the parsed tree

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: In scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts, convert the structural reads to the parser tree and the span map, changing no output bytes: attrOf reads become node.attributes, binding attribute reads to the open tag by construction; the checkStatusFile extractElements/parseAttrs path reads parsed attributes, killing the false status-file-mismatch class on single-quoted legal XML; readRootSnapshot, checkRulingsProvenance and checkCeilingValue read root attributes from the parsed root instead of matching the root open tag; the fenced-metadata scan's outsideBody text replacement becomes a parser walk — any text node outside a Body element that contains a fence fails; elementSpans callers take parser nodes with span-map offsets from computeElementSpans instead of position-paired regex spans; the eligibility scan in validateRecordRetirement is already parser-based (walkNodes) and stays. The dead childInner and childOpenAttrs helpers are deleted. The token readers over prose fields — F_TOKEN_RE over registry Pays cells, the Closed-with clause reader, token extraction from finding bodies, the markdown-table readers — are text processing and are not converted (spec NonGoal). The golden test from T-001 stays green through this task: read conversion alone changes no written byte.

T-005.Title: Convert every structural write to a byte-preserving splice positioned by parser-derived spans, and inherit the equivalence-class probe as a permanent test

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: All seven document mutations keep their splice mechanics and change only their positioning: withStatusRetired rewrites the status attribute inside the open-tag range the span map located; withPaidBy inserts the PaidBy line immediately after the open tag's closing angle bracket; setEntryLayer locates the Entry element by parsed id and rewrites the layer attribute inside that open-tag range; withRootSnapshot rewrites the root's attributes within the root open-tag range; removeSpans removes exactly the parser-derived spans; appendElements inserts before the root close-tag offset instead of a lastIndexOf search. After this task no constructed regex or attrOf call remains in the engine: the reads converted in T-004 removed their last read-side callers and the write conversion removes the rest, and the empty shells are deleted. Byte preservation is the hard requirement and is tested by the T-001 golden comparison staying green: on the fixture move, every file the converted engine writes is byte-identical to the file the shipped engine wrote for the same fixture state — the diff stability, prose bytes and entity forms that citations depend on may not move. No persisted ceiling, base or headroom value changes; persistSnapshot and the newlineCount inputs to the ceiling formulas are untouched.

The equivalence-class probe is inherited as a permanent test in scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts: for the fixture where one live element (f21) is eligible via the C-SELECTION registry row, rewriting that element's open tag as single-quoted attributes, as spaces around the equals signs, or with attributes reordered — each valid XML parsing identically — yields the same validate verdict and the same retire move-set as the unmodified tag: element moved to the retired sibling, stamped, index layer flipped, moved count unchanged. The test drives the real script by spawnSync on isolated temporary roots, covers the unmodified tag as the control, and carries an explicit generous timeout (F185). This test could not pass before T-004 and T-005 — the baseline recorded the shipped engine failing it — which is its discrimination evidence.

T-006.Title: Remove the archived-spec prose pass from derivePayerMap, declare payment structurally, and inherit the false-payment probe as a permanent test

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: The archived-spec sentence pass in derivePayerMap — the loop that flattens each archived spec.xml, splits it into sentences, tests each against the PAID_FINDING_RE pattern and pays every F-token in a matching sentence — is removed, with its pattern constant. After this task the payer map is derived from exactly two declared routes, both already structural: a registry row whose name is an archive directory, via its Pays element; and that row's status text closing clause via the existing Closed-with reader. No archived spec.xml file is read by the payer derivation any more. The real record still validates green: the seven tokens the nine minting sentences name are all retired with stored PaidBy stamps, five have row routes in registry-retired.xml, and F152 and F43 were prose-only routes whose stamps are stored on the retired elements and never re-derived, so removing the pass un-pays nothing and un-retires nothing. No retired element's stamp is rewritten. This overturns part of C-RECORD-RETIREMENT's finding-eligibility constraint exactly as the approved spec argues it; the plan adds no argument of its own.

Two permanent tests join scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts, both using the committed copy scripts/fixtures/record-parse/parked-spec.xml and never the parked branch. First, the false-payment probe, both directions: the fixture record with the parked spec copied in as archive event C-PAYMENT-RECORD-3 leaves every finding that spec refuses to pay live and eligible by no prose route — no finding-eligible-still-live error attributable to a spec sentence — while the same fixture without the copied spec also validates green, so the test discriminates; baseline-probes.json records the shipped engine minting 15 payments here before the fix. Second, the payer derivation over the real record and real archive at this task's base: derivePayerMap's returned map contains no F152 or F43 entry and every other token's payer is unchanged from the baseline map in baseline-probes.json, compared token by token, with an explicit generous timeout as a real-repository measurement (F185). The map is invariant under the archive move: after this bundle archives, its own spec mints by no route, which is what the post-close validator run probes (F196).

T-007.Title: Drive the whole product and pin the byte diffs against the named base commit

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: The full evidence pass, every command exiting 0 as written: both test suites green (bun test src/artifact/xml.test.ts and bun test scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts); the real record validates green (bun ./scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts), which post-close is also the probe that this bundle's own archived spec mints by no route (F196); the two sibling validators green (bun ./scripts/prove-record-preservation.ts and bun ./scripts/validate-citation-anchors.ts); and selected target assertions run (bun ./src/grace.ts lint --path . --change C-RECORD-PARSE --assertions target --run-commands). The three byte-diff pins, each naming 49b4ebb7c6627601ca77ca384f7b6e205d1f65ed in prose and command, each able to fail per the T-001 can-fail demonstration: the seven record paths plus the archive with this bundle's own later arrival excluded; and the docs-and-release surface — README.md, examples/, CLAUDE.md, docs/plans/README.md, skills/ngrace/, plugins/ngrace/skills/ngrace/, package.json and bun.lock. The record files are read, never written, by this bundle: no task edits docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/* and no record file is registered in CONTEXT_ARTIFACTS.
